note: Agents or regimens with a new mechanism, target or modality that are not approved for Richter transformation, selected from major meetings; none of these has a peer-reviewed report in Richter transformation yet. Early response rates often fall with more patients and longer follow-up; meeting data are not peer-reviewed.
scope: No drug is approved specifically for Richter transformation, so most treatments on this page are themselves investigational. This short list holds only agents that have not yet reached a peer-reviewed report; bispecific antibodies, CAR T cells and checkpoint inhibitor combinations with published trials are on the landmark list.

items.why: Most patients now develop Richter transformation during or after a BTK inhibitor. Degrading BTK can work against the mutations that cause resistance to covalent and noncovalent inhibitors.
items.data: CaDAnCe-101, Richter transformation cohort: 7 of 12 evaluable patients responded (58.3%), including 1 complete response (ASH 2024). With 24 patients treated at four dose levels, about half responded, and some responses lasted more than 6 months (ASH 2025).
items.safety: Not reported separately for Richter transformation in the sources used.
items.next: The phase 1/2 trial continues (CaDAnCe-101, NCT05006716). No phase 3 trial in Richter transformation.

items.tgt: CD20 on B cells and CD3 on T cells
items.why: Epcoritamab alone gave responses in 47.6% of patients (EPCORE CLL-1, on the landmark list). Combining it with chemotherapy or lenalidomide aims at more complete responses in first-line and relapsed disease.
items.data: EPCORE CLL-1 combination arms: 11 patients received epcoritamab with lenalidomide and 30 received epcoritamab with R-CHOP; complete responses in more than half of the patients.
items.safety: With lenalidomide: cytokine release syndrome in all patients, neutropenia 82%, thrombocytopenia 73%.
items.next: EPCORE CLL-1 continues (NCT04623541). A randomized trial compares pirtobrutinib plus epcoritamab with R-CHOP (CLLRT2, NCT07917780; see Trials to watch).
